archived_current_metadata_quotations.text:
This note fixes the scope of the page's causal and initial-value content and
the status of its claims; it proves nothing by itself.

- **Model conditions versus physical readings.** Chronology, causality, strong
  causality, global hyperbolicity, achronality, acausality, the Cauchy-set
  property and the existence of time or temporal functions are mathematical
  conditions on a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
  ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]],
  [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]],
  [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). The reading of the
  causal future and past as the model's signalling structure, and of the
  absence of closed causal curves or of a Cauchy set as a failure of
  predictability for the classical model, is adopted in the framework
  postulates ([[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]]); it is not proved
  and not observationally established by the mathematics of this page. A
  model with a closed timelike curve is not "mathematically inconsistent": it
  is a model whose causal structure differs from that of the flat models of
  the examples page.

- **What is proved here.** Conditional deductions inside the stated classes
  of curves and models: the curve calculus of
  [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]], the implication from temporal functions
  to time functions and the exclusion of closed causal curves by a time
  function ([[lem-gr-temporal-functions-and-time-functions]]), the
  extendibility of convergent causal ends and the acausality of Cauchy sets
  ([[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]]), the Minkowski model's global
  hyperbolicity and its inertial Cauchy hypersurfaces
  ([[thm-gr-minkowski-cauchy-and-global-hyperbolicity]]), the flat cylinder's
  failure of chronology, causality and the Cauchy property
  ([[thm-gr-flat-cylinder-closed-timelike-and-no-cauchy-set]]), the open
  slab's incompleteness together with its Cauchy slice and global
  hyperbolicity ([[thm-gr-flat-slab-incomplete-geodesic-and-cauchy-slice]]),
  and the local focusing bound along a geodesic congruence
  ([[thm-gr-timelike-raychaudhuri-and-local-focusing]]). Each is a statement
  about the explicitly displayed model and its curve class.

- **Initial value material.** [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]
  defines initial data $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ and the constraint equations as
  the normal and normal-tangential projections of the field equation;
  [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] proves that data induced by a solution of
  the field equation ([[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]) satisfy the
  constraints, and the normal, induced metric and second fundamental form are
  constructed in
  [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]. The
  page does not assert the converse in any form: the existence of a
  development of given data, its uniqueness, the maximal globally hyperbolic
  development, and the equivalence of global hyperbolicity with the existence
  of a Cauchy hypersurface or of a smooth temporal function with Cauchy
  levels are not proved here. Those statements require the local
  Einstein-matter well-posedness theory, the Gauss-Codazzi relations and
  global causal gluing arguments, and are deferred to the later pages of this
  track (the convex-normal-neighborhood and full symmetric-hyperbolic
  pages). The equivalent component form of the constraints in terms of the
  induced scalar curvature and the divergence of $K$ is deferred with them.

- **Focusing versus singularities.** The Raychaudhuri theorem of this page is
  a local differential inequality along one flow line of a smooth geodesic
  congruence: it bounds the affine parameter range on which the congruence
  remains smooth under the stated hypotheses. It does not assert that the
  spacetime ends, that a singularity theorem holds, or that an
  infinite-curvature point forms. A genuine singularity theorem requires its
  own energy, causality and global compactness hypotheses and a complete
  proof, none of which is claimed here; cosmic censorship and chronology
  protection are not theorems and are not used.

- **Empirical status.** The page contains no experiment, no apparatus, no
  measured input, no sampling model and no statistical inference, and it
  draws no conclusion about nature. A prediction computed from a fully
  specified model may later be compared with reported observations; such a
  comparison tests the combined model and its auxiliary assumptions, and
  agreement is evidence, not a proof of the model or of its postulates.

- **Deferred obligations.** The causal hierarchy's equivalences, the

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$

$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition

model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no

parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $h$ be a smooth positive
definite metric on $M$ such that $(M,d_h)$ is complete in each connected
component and every closed $d_h$-bounded subset is compact (both hold for the
metric $h'$ of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]).

**(a) Compact parameter intervals.** Let $T>0$ and let
$\alpha_k:[0,T]\to M$ be future causal curves
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) parametrized by $h$-arclength,
$\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for all $0\le s\le t\le T$, with
$\alpha_k(0)\to p\in M$. Then some subsequence (still written $\alpha_k$)
converges uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,T]$ to a map
$\alpha:[0,T]\to M$ with:

**(a1)** $\alpha(0)=p$ and $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le|t-s|$ for all
$s,t\in[0,T]$;

**(a2)** $\alpha$ is a geodesically connectible continuous causal curve in
the sense of [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]];

**(a3)** $\alpha$ is a future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]; and for every chart $U$ of the
kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (b), with
domination constant $K$ and time coordinate $x^0$, there is a constant
$C\ge1$, depending only on the chart and $h$, such that
$$t-s\le C\bigl(x^0(\alpha(t))-x^0(\alpha(s))\bigr)$$
whenever $s<t$ and $\alpha([s,t])\subseteq U$;

**(a4)** $\alpha$ is not constant on any nondegenerate parameter interval.

**(b) Half-lines.** Let $\gamma_k:I_k\to M$ be future causal curves
parametrized by $h$-arclength whose intervals $I_k\ni0$ satisfy
$[0,n]\subseteq I_k$ for every $k$ once $n$ is fixed (for instance
$I_k=[0,b_k]$ with $b_k\to\infty$), and suppose $\gamma_k(0)\to p$. Then
some subsequence converges uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of
$[0,\infty)$ to a future causal curve $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ satisfying
(a1)-(a4) on compact subintervals and which is future-inextendible
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d)). A dual statement
holds, in the time-reversed orientation, for curves whose intervals satisfy
$[-n,0]\subseteq I_k$ eventually; it produces a past-inextendible future
causal curve on $(-\infty,0]$ in the original orientation.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$F\subseteq M$ be an open future set, so that $I^+(F)=F$
([[def-gr-future-and-past-sets]] clause (a)), and let $A:=\partial F$ be its
achronal boundary. Then:

**(a) Achronality.** $A$ is closed and achronal: no two distinct points of
$A$ are chronologically related in either direction. Consequently every
future or past timelike curve meets $A$ in at most one point.

**(b) Local Lipschitz graph.** For every $p\in A$ there are a chart
$(U,x)$ of the kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a)
and (d) around $p$, with $x(p)=0$ and constants $K$ and $c$, and numbers
$a,\rho>0$ with $W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$, such
that for every $z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$$L_z:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$$
meets $A\cap W$ in exactly one point, and there is a function
$\varphi:B_\rho(0)\to(-a,a)$ with
$$A\cap W=\bigl\{x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z):z\in B_\rho(0)\bigr\},\qquad |\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\quad (z,z'\in B_\rho(0)).$$
Thus $A$ is locally the graph of a Lipschitz function of the spatial
coordinates of the chart.

**(c) Topological hypersurface.** The maps $z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ of
(b), for all points $p\in A$, form a topological atlas on $A$: $A$ is a
topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology and its inclusion into $M$
is a topological embedding. No smoothness of $A$ is asserted.

**(d) Null measure.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mu$ be a measure on the Borel sets of $M$
which is locally absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure:
whenever $(V,y)$ is a chart and $E\subseteq V$ has $y(E)$ of four-dimensional
Lebesgue measure zero, then $\mu(E)=0$. Then $\mu(A\cap K)=0$ for every
compact $K\subseteq M$. In particular this holds for every smooth positive
volume density on $M$.

([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)): every
inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has
$\gamma^{-1}[S]=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$ of exactly one element. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\delta:[a,b]\to M$

the three sets $I^-(S)$, $S$, $I^+(S)$ are pairwise disjoint with
$$M=I^-(S)\;\sqcup\;S\;\sqcup\;I^+(S);$$
moreover for $x\notin S$ one has $x\in I^+(S)$ if and only if some point of

[[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (d) around $p$, with

$$|\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\qquad(z,z'\in B_\rho(0)),$$
with $\varphi(0)=0$ and $|\varphi(z)|\le\sqrt c\,|z|<a$. The cylinder $W$ may be chosen inside any prescribed neighborhood of $p$. Consequently the maps

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $h$ be the auxiliary
metric of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]], so that
$(M,d_h)$ is complete and closed $d_h$-bounded sets are compact. Let
$$\alpha_k:[0,b_k]\to M,\qquad 0<b_k<\infty,$$
be future causal curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]])
parametrized by $h$-arclength, $\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for
$0\le s\le t\le b_k$, with $\alpha_k(0)\to x\in M$ and
$\alpha_k(b_k)\to z\in M$. Passing to a subsequence, let
$b:=\lim_kb_k\in[0,\infty]$. Then:

**(i) Bounded case.** If $b<\infty$, there is a subsequence and a future causal
curve $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=x$, $\alpha(b)=z$ and
$d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le t-s$ for $s\le t$, such that the subsequence
converges to $\alpha$ uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,b]$. If $b=0$ then $x=z$ and
$\alpha$ is the constant curve at $x$.

**(ii) Unbounded case.** If $b=\infty$, there are a future-inextendible future
causal curve $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ with $\alpha^+(0)=x$ and a
past-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ with
$\alpha^-(0)=z$, such that a subsequence converges to $\alpha^+$ uniformly on
every compact subinterval of $[0,\infty)$ and to $\alpha^-$ uniformly on every
compact subinterval of $(-\infty,0]$ (where $\alpha^-$ is the limit of the
curves $s\mapsto\alpha_k(b_k+s)$, $s\le0$, for large $k$). Moreover for all
$t_+\ge0$ and $t_-\le0$ there are parameters $u_k\le v_k$ with
$u_k\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and $v_k\to\alpha^-(t_-)$; in particular
$(\alpha^+(t_+),\alpha^-(t_-))$ lies in the closure of the causal relation in
the strong sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (c):
there exist sequences $u_j\le v_j$ with $u_j\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and
$v_j\to\alpha^-(t_-)$.

**(iii) Coincident endpoints.** If $x=z$, then in case (i) with $b>0$ the
curve $\alpha$ is a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $x$
($\alpha(0)=\alpha(b)=x$), and in case (ii) the concatenation $\gamma$ of
$\alpha^-$ and $\alpha^+$ is an inextendible future causal curve
$\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ with $\gamma(0)=x$.

**(iv) Imprisonment.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be strongly causal
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (b)) and
suppose all images $\alpha_k([0,b_k])$ are contained in one compact set $K$.
Then $b\le L(K)<\infty$ where $L(K)$ is the length bound of
[[lem-gr-strong-causality-compact-length-bound]]; in particular the case
$b=\infty$ is excluded.

equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by

take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;

  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with

cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be two developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]].

**(a) Common subdevelopment.** A **common subdevelopment** of $M$ and $M'$ is
a pair $(U,\varphi)$ in which

1. $U\subseteq M$ is an open subset with $j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$ such that the
   restriction $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ is a development of the same data
   (with the induced field equations on the open submanifold $U$); and
2. $\varphi:(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)\to(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a development
   embedding in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
   clause (c).

Here "the induced field equations on $U$" means the equations of clause (a)4
of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] restricted to $U$; the
induced Lorentzian manifold is $(U,g|_U)$ with the time orientation $N|_U$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(b) Maximal common development.** A common subdevelopment $(U^*,\varphi^*)$
is a **maximal common development** (MCD) of $M$ and $M'$ when for every
common subdevelopment $(U,\varphi)$ one has $U\subseteq U^*$ and
$\varphi^*|_U=\varphi$. Existence is not asserted by this definition; it is
proved in [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]].

**(c) Corresponding boundary points.** Let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common
subdevelopment. Its **corresponding boundary points** are pairs
$(p,p')\in\partial^M U\times\partial^{M'}\varphi(U)$, where the boundaries are
taken in $M$ and in $M'$ respectively, such that for every open neighbourhood
$V$ of $p$ in $M$ and every open neighbourhood $V'$ of $p'$ in $M'$ there is
$x\in V\cap U$ with $\varphi(x)\in V'$.

**(d) Side of the initial surface.** For a corresponding pair $(p,p')$: if
$V,V'$ range over a base of neighbourhoods, the condition of (c) forces every
$x$ witnessing it to lie on one side of $j(\Sigma)$: either $x\in I^+(j(\Sigma))$
for cofinally many witnesses, or $x\in I^-(j(\Sigma))$ for cofinally many
witnesses, but not both, since $I^\pm(j(\Sigma))$ are open and determined by
the trichotomy of [[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]]. The corresponding
pair is then said to lie to the **future** or to the **past** of the initial
surface; the future case is the one used in this batch, the past case being
its time reverse.

**(e) Scope.** These are mathematical relations between two fixed developments
and their boundary points. Neither the existence of boundary points, nor the
existence of a common subdevelopment with nonempty boundary, nor uniqueness of
a corresponding point, is asserted here.

inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\in J^+(q)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be two developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]].

**(a) Common subdevelopment.** A **common subdevelopment** of $M$ and $M'$ is
a pair $(U,\varphi)$ in which

1. $U\subseteq M$ is an open subset with $j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$ such that the
   restriction $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ is a development of the same data
   (with the induced field equations on the open submanifold $U$); and
2. $\varphi:(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)\to(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a development
   embedding in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
   clause (c).

Here "the induced field equations on $U$" means the equations of clause (a)4
of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] restricted to $U$; the
induced Lorentzian manifold is $(U,g|_U)$ with the time orientation $N|_U$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(b) Maximal common development.** A common subdevelopment $(U^*,\varphi^*)$
is a **maximal common development** (MCD) of $M$ and $M'$ when for every
common subdevelopment $(U,\varphi)$ one has $U\subseteq U^*$ and
$\varphi^*|_U=\varphi$. Existence is not asserted by this definition; it is
proved in [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]].

subdevelopment. Its **corresponding boundary points** are pairs
$(p,p')\in\partial^M U\times\partial^{M'}\varphi(U)$, where the boundaries are
taken in $M$ and in $M'$ respectively, such that for every open neighbourhood
$V$ of $p$ in $M$ and every open neighbourhood $V'$ of $p'$ in $M'$ there is
$x\in V\cap U$ with $\varphi(x)\in V'$.

**(d) Side of the initial surface.** For a corresponding pair $(p,p')$: if
$V,V'$ range over a base of neighbourhoods, the condition of (c) forces every
$x$ witnessing it to lie on one side of $j(\Sigma)$: either $x\in I^+(j(\Sigma))$
for cofinally many witnesses, or $x\in I^-(j(\Sigma))$ for cofinally many
witnesses, but not both, since $I^\pm(j(\Sigma))$ are open and determined by
the trichotomy of [[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]]. The corresponding
pair is then said to lie to the **future** or to the **past** of the initial
surface; the future case is the one used in this batch, the past case being
its time reverse.

**(e) Scope.** These are mathematical relations between two fixed developments
and their boundary points. Neither the existence of boundary points, nor the
existence of a common subdevelopment with nonempty boundary, nor uniqueness of
a corresponding point, is asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)): every
inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has
$\gamma^{-1}[S]=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$ of exactly one element. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\delta:[a,b]\to M$
with $\delta(a)=\delta(b)$; in particular $S$ is achronal and acausal, and
the three sets $I^-(S)$, $S$, $I^+(S)$ are pairwise disjoint with
$$M=I^-(S)\;\sqcup\;S\;\sqcup\;I^+(S);$$
moreover for $x\notin S$ one has $x\in I^+(S)$ if and only if some point of
$S$ chronologically precedes $x$;

**(b)** $S$ is closed in $M$;

[[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (d) around $p$, with
$x(p)=0$ and the supplier constants $K\ge1$ and $c=16$, and numbers $a,\rho,\eta>0$ with $\sqrt c\,\rho+\eta<a$ and
$W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$ such that for every
$z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$L_z=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$ meets $S\cap W$ in exactly one
point $x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$, and
$$|\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\qquad(z,z'\in B_\rho(0)),$$
with $\varphi(0)=0$ and $|\varphi(z)|\le\sqrt c\,|z|<a$. The cylinder $W$ may be chosen inside any prescribed neighborhood of $p$. Consequently the maps
$z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ form a topological atlas on the closed set
$S$, making $S$ a topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology whose
inclusion into $M$ is a topological embedding.

([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $h$ be the auxiliary
metric of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]], so that

be future causal curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]])
parametrized by $h$-arclength, $\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for

curve $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=x$, $\alpha(b)=z$ and
$d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le t-s$ for $s\le t$, such that the subsequence
converges to $\alpha$ uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,b]$. If $b=0$ then $x=z$ and
$\alpha$ is the constant curve at $x$.

causal curve $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ with $\alpha^+(0)=x$ and a
past-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ with
$\alpha^-(0)=z$, such that a subsequence converges to $\alpha^+$ uniformly on
every compact subinterval of $[0,\infty)$ and to $\alpha^-$ uniformly on every
compact subinterval of $(-\infty,0]$ (where $\alpha^-$ is the limit of the
curves $s\mapsto\alpha_k(b_k+s)$, $s\le0$, for large $k$). Moreover for all
$t_+\ge0$ and $t_-\le0$ there are parameters $u_k\le v_k$ with
$u_k\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and $v_k\to\alpha^-(t_-)$; in particular
$(\alpha^+(t_+),\alpha^-(t_-))$ lies in the closure of the causal relation in
the strong sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (c):
there exist sequences $u_j\le v_j$ with $u_j\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and
$v_j\to\alpha^-(t_-)$.

curve $\alpha$ is a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $x$
($\alpha(0)=\alpha(b)=x$), and in case (ii) the concatenation $\gamma$ of
$\alpha^-$ and $\alpha^+$ is an inextendible future causal curve
$\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ with $\gamma(0)=x$.

([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (b)) and

[[lem-gr-strong-causality-compact-length-bound]]; in particular the case
$b=\infty$ is excluded.

([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.

required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition

model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that

irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\in J^+(q)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be two developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]].

**(a) Common subdevelopment.** A **common subdevelopment** of $M$ and $M'$ is
a pair $(U,\varphi)$ in which

1. $U\subseteq M$ is an open subset with $j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$ such that the
   restriction $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ is a development of the same data
   (with the induced field equations on the open submanifold $U$); and
2. $\varphi:(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)\to(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a development
   embedding in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
   clause (c).

Here "the induced field equations on $U$" means the equations of clause (a)4
of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] restricted to $U$; the
induced Lorentzian manifold is $(U,g|_U)$ with the time orientation $N|_U$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(b) Maximal common development.** A common subdevelopment $(U^*,\varphi^*)$
is a **maximal common development** (MCD) of $M$ and $M'$ when for every
common subdevelopment $(U,\varphi)$ one has $U\subseteq U^*$ and
$\varphi^*|_U=\varphi$. Existence is not asserted by this definition; it is
proved in [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]].

**(c) Corresponding boundary points.** Let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common
subdevelopment. Its **corresponding boundary points** are pairs
$(p,p')\in\partial^M U\times\partial^{M'}\varphi(U)$, where the boundaries are
taken in $M$ and in $M'$ respectively, such that for every open neighbourhood
$V$ of $p$ in $M$ and every open neighbourhood $V'$ of $p'$ in $M'$ there is
$x\in V\cap U$ with $\varphi(x)\in V'$.

**(d) Side of the initial surface.** For a corresponding pair $(p,p')$: if
$V,V'$ range over a base of neighbourhoods, the condition of (c) forces every
$x$ witnessing it to lie on one side of $j(\Sigma)$: either $x\in I^+(j(\Sigma))$
for cofinally many witnesses, or $x\in I^-(j(\Sigma))$ for cofinally many
witnesses, but not both, since $I^\pm(j(\Sigma))$ are open and determined by
the trichotomy of [[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]]. The corresponding
pair is then said to lie to the **future** or to the **past** of the initial
surface; the future case is the one used in this batch, the past case being
its time reverse.

**(e) Scope.** These are mathematical relations between two fixed developments
and their boundary points. Neither the existence of boundary points, nor the
existence of a common subdevelopment with nonempty boundary, nor uniqueness of
a corresponding point, is asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)): every
inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has
$\gamma^{-1}[S]=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$ of exactly one element. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\delta:[a,b]\to M$
with $\delta(a)=\delta(b)$; in particular $S$ is achronal and acausal, and
the three sets $I^-(S)$, $S$, $I^+(S)$ are pairwise disjoint with
$$M=I^-(S)\;\sqcup\;S\;\sqcup\;I^+(S);$$
moreover for $x\notin S$ one has $x\in I^+(S)$ if and only if some point of
$S$ chronologically precedes $x$;

**(b)** $S$ is closed in $M$;

**(c)** for every $p\in S$ there are a chart $(U,x)$ of the kind produced by
[[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (d) around $p$, with
$x(p)=0$ and the supplier constants $K\ge1$ and $c=16$, and numbers $a,\rho,\eta>0$ with $\sqrt c\,\rho+\eta<a$ and
$W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$ such that for every
$z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$L_z=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$ meets $S\cap W$ in exactly one
point $x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$, and
$$|\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\qquad(z,z'\in B_\rho(0)),$$
with $\varphi(0)=0$ and $|\varphi(z)|\le\sqrt c\,|z|<a$. The cylinder $W$ may be chosen inside any prescribed neighborhood of $p$. Consequently the maps
$z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ form a topological atlas on the closed set
$S$, making $S$ a topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology whose
inclusion into $M$ is a topological embedding.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), and let
$t$ be the volume time function of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]]. Then
there exist a smooth function $T:M\to\mathbb R$ and, with $\nabla T$ the
gradient of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], the
following hold.

**(a)** $T$ is a temporal function in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (e): smooth,
$g(\nabla T,\nabla T)<0$ and $g(\nabla T,N)>0$ everywhere.

**(b)** Every level set $S_c:=T^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is a Cauchy
hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clauses (a)
and (c)): it is a spacelike embedded hypersurface and every inextendible
causal curve meets it in exactly one parameter value. In particular $T$ is
surjective.

**(c)** Along every inextendible future-directed causal curve
$T\to+\infty$, and along every inextendible past-directed causal curve
$T\to-\infty$.

**(d)** The vector field $X:=\nabla T/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$ is smooth,
future-directed timelike, satisfies $X(T)=1$, and is complete
([[def-complete-vector-field]]): every maximal integral curve of $X$ is
defined on all of $\mathbb R$, so by
[[prop-a-vector-field-is-complete-if-and-only-if-its-flow-is-global]] its
flow $\Phi:\mathbb R\times M\to M$ is a global smooth flow
([[def-local-and-global-flow]]).

**(e)** The map $\Psi:\mathbb R\times S_0\to M$, $\Psi(s,z):=\Phi(s,z)$, is
a diffeomorphism and $T(\Psi(s,z))=s$ for all $(s,z)$; equivalently $M$ is
foliated by the Cauchy hypersurfaces $S_c$, each flow line meeting each level
exactly once.

**(f)** Put $\beta:=-1/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$, a smooth positive function, and
$h_T:=g+\beta\,dT\otimes dT$. Then $g=-\beta\,dT\otimes dT+h_T$;
$h_T(X,\cdot)=0$; and $h_T$ restricted to $\ker dT$ is a smooth Riemannian
metric, so the decomposition $T_pM=\mathbb RX_p\oplus\ker dT_p$ is
$g$-orthogonal with $g(X,X)=-\beta$. Consequently the pullback of $g$ by the
diffeomorphism $\Psi$ has no mixed terms,
$$\Psi^*g=-(\beta\circ\Psi)\,ds^2+h,\qquad h_{(s,z)}(v,w):=g_{\Phi(s,z)}\bigl((d\Phi_s)_zv,(d\Phi_s)_zw\bigr),$$
a sum of a negative definite one-dimensional form and the smooth family of
Riemannian metrics induced on the levels.

classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],

**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with

continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].

in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently

([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be two developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]].

a pair $(U,\varphi)$ in which

1. $U\subseteq M$ is an open subset with $j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$ such that the
   restriction $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ is a development of the same data
   (with the induced field equations on the open submanifold $U$); and
2. $\varphi:(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)\to(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a development
   embedding in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
   clause (c).

of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] restricted to $U$; the
induced Lorentzian manifold is $(U,g|_U)$ with the time orientation $N|_U$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

is a **maximal common development** (MCD) of $M$ and $M'$ when for every
common subdevelopment $(U,\varphi)$ one has $U\subseteq U^*$ and
$\varphi^*|_U=\varphi$. Existence is not asserted by this definition; it is
proved in [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]].

subdevelopment. Its **corresponding boundary points** are pairs
$(p,p')\in\partial^M U\times\partial^{M'}\varphi(U)$, where the boundaries are
taken in $M$ and in $M'$ respectively, such that for every open neighbourhood
$V$ of $p$ in $M$ and every open neighbourhood $V'$ of $p'$ in $M'$ there is
$x\in V\cap U$ with $\varphi(x)\in V'$.

$V,V'$ range over a base of neighbourhoods, the condition of (c) forces every
$x$ witnessing it to lie on one side of $j(\Sigma)$: either $x\in I^+(j(\Sigma))$
for cofinally many witnesses, or $x\in I^-(j(\Sigma))$ for cofinally many
witnesses, but not both, since $I^\pm(j(\Sigma))$ are open and determined by
the trichotomy of [[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]]. The corresponding
pair is then said to lie to the **future** or to the **past** of the initial
surface; the future case is the one used in this batch, the past case being
its time reverse.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold

classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$

[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in

locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which

$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.

required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point

  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and

curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

This note fixes the scope of the page's causal and initial-value content and
the status of its claims; it proves nothing by itself.

- **Model conditions versus physical readings.** Chronology, causality, strong
  causality, global hyperbolicity, achronality, acausality, the Cauchy-set
  property and the existence of time or temporal functions are mathematical
  conditions on a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
  ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]],
  [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]],
  [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). The reading of the
  causal future and past as the model's signalling structure, and of the
  absence of closed causal curves or of a Cauchy set as a failure of
  predictability for the classical model, is adopted in the framework
  postulates ([[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]]); it is not proved
  and not observationally established by the mathematics of this page. A
  model with a closed timelike curve is not "mathematically inconsistent": it
  is a model whose causal structure differs from that of the flat models of
  the examples page.

- **What is proved here.** Conditional deductions inside the stated classes
  of curves and models: the curve calculus of
  [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]], the implication from temporal functions
  to time functions and the exclusion of closed causal curves by a time
  function ([[lem-gr-temporal-functions-and-time-functions]]), the
  extendibility of convergent causal ends and the acausality of Cauchy sets
  ([[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]]), the Minkowski model's global
  hyperbolicity and its inertial Cauchy hypersurfaces
  ([[thm-gr-minkowski-cauchy-and-global-hyperbolicity]]), the flat cylinder's
  failure of chronology, causality and the Cauchy property
  ([[thm-gr-flat-cylinder-closed-timelike-and-no-cauchy-set]]), the open
  slab's incompleteness together with its Cauchy slice and global
  hyperbolicity ([[thm-gr-flat-slab-incomplete-geodesic-and-cauchy-slice]]),
  and the local focusing bound along a geodesic congruence
  ([[thm-gr-timelike-raychaudhuri-and-local-focusing]]). Each is a statement
  about the explicitly displayed model and its curve class.

- **Initial value material.** [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]
  defines initial data $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ and the constraint equations as
  the normal and normal-tangential projections of the field equation;
  [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] proves that data induced by a solution of
  the field equation ([[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]) satisfy the
  constraints, and the normal, induced metric and second fundamental form are
  constructed in
  [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]. The
  page does not assert the converse in any form: the existence of a
  development of given data, its uniqueness, the maximal globally hyperbolic
  development, and the equivalence of global hyperbolicity with the existence
  of a Cauchy hypersurface or of a smooth temporal function with Cauchy
  levels are not proved here. Those statements require the local
  Einstein-matter well-posedness theory, the Gauss-Codazzi relations and
  global causal gluing arguments, and are deferred to the later pages of this
  track (the convex-normal-neighborhood and full symmetric-hyperbolic
  pages). The equivalent component form of the constraints in terms of the
  induced scalar curvature and the divergence of $K$ is deferred with them.

- **Focusing versus singularities.** The Raychaudhuri theorem of this page is
  a local differential inequality along one flow line of a smooth geodesic
  congruence: it bounds the affine parameter range on which the congruence
  remains smooth under the stated hypotheses. It does not assert that the
  spacetime ends, that a singularity theorem holds, or that an
  infinite-curvature point forms. A genuine singularity theorem requires its
  own energy, causality and global compactness hypotheses and a complete
  proof, none of which is claimed here; cosmic censorship and chronology
  protection are not theorems and are not used.

- **Empirical status.** The page contains no experiment, no apparatus, no
  measured input, no sampling model and no statistical inference, and it
  draws no conclusion about nature. A prediction computed from a fully
  specified model may later be compared with reported observations; such a
  comparison tests the combined model and its auxiliary assumptions, and
  agreement is evidence, not a proof of the model or of its postulates.

- **Deferred obligations.** The causal hierarchy's equivalences, the
  equivalence of the global-hyperbolicity formulation used here with the
  Cauchy-hypersurface and smooth-splitting formulations, the existence and
  uniqueness theory for the Einstein-matter initial value problem, the
  maximal development, and singularity and censorship statements are
  obligations of the later pages of the general-relativity track, not of this
  page.

convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in

curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;

  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$

versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\in J^+(q)\}$ and

model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $h$ be a smooth positive
definite metric on $M$ such that $(M,d_h)$ is complete in each connected
component and every closed $d_h$-bounded subset is compact (both hold for the
metric $h'$ of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]).

**(a) Compact parameter intervals.** Let $T>0$ and let
$\alpha_k:[0,T]\to M$ be future causal curves
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) parametrized by $h$-arclength,
$\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for all $0\le s\le t\le T$, with
$\alpha_k(0)\to p\in M$. Then some subsequence (still written $\alpha_k$)
converges uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,T]$ to a map
$\alpha:[0,T]\to M$ with:

**(a1)** $\alpha(0)=p$ and $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le|t-s|$ for all
$s,t\in[0,T]$;

**(a2)** $\alpha$ is a geodesically connectible continuous causal curve in
the sense of [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]];

**(a3)** $\alpha$ is a future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]; and for every chart $U$ of the
kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (b), with
domination constant $K$ and time coordinate $x^0$, there is a constant
$C\ge1$, depending only on the chart and $h$, such that
$$t-s\le C\bigl(x^0(\alpha(t))-x^0(\alpha(s))\bigr)$$
whenever $s<t$ and $\alpha([s,t])\subseteq U$;

**(a4)** $\alpha$ is not constant on any nondegenerate parameter interval.

**(b) Half-lines.** Let $\gamma_k:I_k\to M$ be future causal curves
parametrized by $h$-arclength whose intervals $I_k\ni0$ satisfy
$[0,n]\subseteq I_k$ for every $k$ once $n$ is fixed (for instance
$I_k=[0,b_k]$ with $b_k\to\infty$), and suppose $\gamma_k(0)\to p$. Then
some subsequence converges uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of
$[0,\infty)$ to a future causal curve $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ satisfying
(a1)-(a4) on compact subintervals and which is future-inextendible
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d)). A dual statement
holds, in the time-reversed orientation, for curves whose intervals satisfy
$[-n,0]\subseteq I_k$ eventually; it produces a past-inextendible future
causal curve on $(-\infty,0]$ in the original orientation.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$F\subseteq M$ be an open future set, so that $I^+(F)=F$
([[def-gr-future-and-past-sets]] clause (a)), and let $A:=\partial F$ be its
achronal boundary. Then:

**(a) Achronality.** $A$ is closed and achronal: no two distinct points of
$A$ are chronologically related in either direction. Consequently every
future or past timelike curve meets $A$ in at most one point.

**(b) Local Lipschitz graph.** For every $p\in A$ there are a chart
$(U,x)$ of the kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a)
and (d) around $p$, with $x(p)=0$ and constants $K$ and $c$, and numbers
$a,\rho>0$ with $W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$, such
that for every $z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$$L_z:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$$
meets $A\cap W$ in exactly one point, and there is a function
$\varphi:B_\rho(0)\to(-a,a)$ with
$$A\cap W=\bigl\{x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z):z\in B_\rho(0)\bigr\},\qquad |\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\quad (z,z'\in B_\rho(0)).$$
Thus $A$ is locally the graph of a Lipschitz function of the spatial
coordinates of the chart.

**(c) Topological hypersurface.** The maps $z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ of
(b), for all points $p\in A$, form a topological atlas on $A$: $A$ is a
topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology and its inclusion into $M$
is a topological embedding. No smoothness of $A$ is asserted.

**(d) Null measure.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mu$ be a measure on the Borel sets of $M$
which is locally absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure:
whenever $(V,y)$ is a chart and $E\subseteq V$ has $y(E)$ of four-dimensional
Lebesgue measure zero, then $\mu(E)=0$. Then $\mu(A\cap K)=0$ for every
compact $K\subseteq M$. In particular this holds for every smooth positive
volume density on $M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)): every
inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has
$\gamma^{-1}[S]=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$ of exactly one element. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\delta:[a,b]\to M$
with $\delta(a)=\delta(b)$; in particular $S$ is achronal and acausal, and
the three sets $I^-(S)$, $S$, $I^+(S)$ are pairwise disjoint with
$$M=I^-(S)\;\sqcup\;S\;\sqcup\;I^+(S);$$
moreover for $x\notin S$ one has $x\in I^+(S)$ if and only if some point of
$S$ chronologically precedes $x$;

**(b)** $S$ is closed in $M$;

**(c)** for every $p\in S$ there are a chart $(U,x)$ of the kind produced by
[[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (d) around $p$, with
$x(p)=0$ and constants $K$ and $c$, and numbers $a,\rho>0$ with
$W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$ such that for every
$z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$L_z=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$ meets $S\cap W$ in exactly one
point $x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$, and
$$|\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\qquad(z,z'\in B_\rho(0)),$$
with $|\varphi(z)|<1+\sqrt c\,|z|<a$. Consequently the maps
$z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ form a topological atlas on the closed set
$S$, making $S$ a topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology whose
inclusion into $M$ is a topological embedding.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $h$ be the auxiliary
metric of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]], so that
$(M,d_h)$ is complete and closed $d_h$-bounded sets are compact. Let
$$\alpha_k:[0,b_k]\to M,\qquad 0<b_k<\infty,$$
be future causal curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]])
parametrized by $h$-arclength, $\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for
$0\le s\le t\le b_k$, with $\alpha_k(0)\to x\in M$ and
$\alpha_k(b_k)\to z\in M$. Passing to a subsequence, let
$b:=\lim_kb_k\in[0,\infty]$. Then:

**(i) Bounded case.** If $b<\infty$, there is a subsequence and a future causal
curve $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=x$, $\alpha(b)=z$ and
$d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le t-s$ for $s\le t$, such that the subsequence
converges to $\alpha$ uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,b]$. If $b=0$ then $x=z$ and
$\alpha$ is the constant curve at $x$.

**(ii) Unbounded case.** If $b=\infty$, there are a future-inextendible future
causal curve $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ with $\alpha^+(0)=x$ and a
past-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ with
$\alpha^-(0)=z$, such that a subsequence converges to $\alpha^+$ uniformly on
every compact subinterval of $[0,\infty)$ and to $\alpha^-$ uniformly on every
compact subinterval of $(-\infty,0]$ (where $\alpha^-$ is the limit of the
curves $s\mapsto\alpha_k(b_k+s)$, $s\le0$, for large $k$). Moreover for all
$t_+\ge0$ and $t_-\le0$ there are parameters $u_k\le v_k$ with
$u_k\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and $v_k\to\alpha^-(t_-)$; in particular
$(\alpha^+(t_+),\alpha^-(t_-))$ lies in the closure of the causal relation in
the strong sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (c):
there exist sequences $u_j\le v_j$ with $u_j\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and
$v_j\to\alpha^-(t_-)$.

**(iii) Coincident endpoints.** If $x=z$, then in case (i) with $b>0$ the
curve $\alpha$ is a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $x$
($\alpha(0)=\alpha(b)=x$), and in case (ii) the concatenation $\gamma$ of
$\alpha^-$ and $\alpha^+$ is an inextendible future causal curve
$\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ with $\gamma(0)=x$.

**(iv) Imprisonment.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be strongly causal
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (b)) and
suppose all images $\alpha_k([0,b_k])$ are contained in one compact set $K$.
Then $b\le L(K)<\infty$ where $L(K)$ is the length bound of
[[lem-gr-strong-causality-compact-length-bound]]; in particular the case
$b=\infty$ is excluded.

**(a)** $\tau=-1$ on $\{t\le a\}$;

**(b)** $\tau=+1$ on $\{t\ge c\}$;

**(c)** $\nabla\tau$ is past causal or zero at every point of $M$: with the
gradient of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] one has
$g(\nabla\tau,\nabla\tau)\le0$ and $d\tau(N)=g(\nabla\tau,N)\ge0$;

**(d)** $\nabla\tau$ is past timelike at every point of $S_b$ and hence, by
continuity, on an open neighborhood of $S_b$: $g(\nabla\tau,\nabla\tau)<0$
and $g(\nabla\tau,N)>0$ there.

everywhere.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), and let
$t$ be the volume time function of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]]. Then
there exist a smooth function $T:M\to\mathbb R$ and, with $\nabla T$ the
gradient of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], the
following hold.

**(a)** $T$ is a temporal function in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (e): smooth,
$g(\nabla T,\nabla T)<0$ and $g(\nabla T,N)>0$ everywhere.

**(b)** Every level set $S_c:=T^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is a Cauchy
hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clauses (a)
and (c)): it is a spacelike embedded hypersurface and every inextendible
causal curve meets it in exactly one parameter value. In particular $T$ is
surjective.

**(c)** Along every inextendible future-directed causal curve
$T\to+\infty$, and along every inextendible past-directed causal curve
$T\to-\infty$.

**(d)** The vector field $X:=\nabla T/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$ is smooth,
future-directed timelike, satisfies $X(T)=1$, and is complete
([[def-complete-vector-field]]): every maximal integral curve of $X$ is
defined on all of $\mathbb R$, so by
[[prop-a-vector-field-is-complete-if-and-only-if-its-flow-is-global]] its
flow $\Phi:\mathbb R\times M\to M$ is a global smooth flow
([[def-local-and-global-flow]]).

**(e)** The map $\Psi:\mathbb R\times S_0\to M$, $\Psi(s,z):=\Phi(s,z)$, is
a diffeomorphism and $T(\Psi(s,z))=s$ for all $(s,z)$; equivalently $M$ is
foliated by the Cauchy hypersurfaces $S_c$, each flow line meeting each level
exactly once.

**(f)** Put $\beta:=-1/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$, a smooth positive function, and
$h_T:=g+\beta\,dT\otimes dT$. Then $g=-\beta\,dT\otimes dT+h_T$;
$h_T(X,\cdot)=0$; and $h_T$ restricted to $\ker dT$ is a smooth Riemannian
metric, so the decomposition $T_pM=\mathbb RX_p\oplus\ker dT_p$ is
$g$-orthogonal with $g(X,X)=-\beta$. Consequently the pullback of $g$ by the
diffeomorphism $\Psi$ has no mixed terms,
$$\Psi^*g=-(\beta\circ\Psi)\,ds^2+h,\qquad h_{(s,z)}(v,w):=g_{\Phi(s,z)}\bigl((d\Phi_s)_zv,(d\Phi_s)_zw\bigr),$$
a sum of a negative definite one-dimensional form and the smooth family of
Riemannian metrics induced on the levels.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\in J^+(q)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.
